claim: BEST-Route jointly selects which LLM to route a query to AND how many samples to draw (best-of-n) from that model, based on predicted query difficulty and a quality threshold.
scope_conditions: real-world query datasets, whole-query granularity, ICML 2025
quoted_support: We leverage this idea to propose BEST-Route, a novel routing framework that chooses a model and the number of responses to sample from it based on query difficulty and the quality thresholds.

claim: Prior query routing approaches that generate only a single response from the selected small model often fail to beat a single large-model response, causing routers to overuse the large model and lose potential cost savings.
scope_conditions: general LLM query routing literature pre-2025
quoted_support: a single response from a small (inexpensive) model was often not good enough to beat a response from a large (expensive) model due to which they end up overusing the large model and missing out on potential cost savings.

claim: Routing plus compute-allocation research treats the query as an atomic unit; no published routing method allocates different models or sample budgets to different sub-parts (requirements) of a single task.
stance_target: novelty of per-requirement cross-model routing (candidate c)
quoted_support: Large language models (LLMs) are powerful tools but are often expensive to deploy at scale. LLM query routing mitigates this by dynamically assigning queries to models of varying cost and quality to obtain a desired trade-off.
